newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African team to consider Pretoria's help in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: S.African team to consider Pretoria's help in Zaire.

text.p: South African government and military officials will go to Tanzania on Thursday to assess how Pretoria can contribute to a humanitarian force for Central Africa, the department of foreign affairs said on Wednesday.

"The visit will underline South Africa's commitment to play an active role in international efforts to alleviate the humanitarian crisis of catastrophic proportions in the region and in the long run to bring lasting peace to the countries involved," a statement said.
President Nelson Mandela said on Monday he was prepared to send troops to Central Africa as part of an international force, but he needed more information to decide how many to commit.
The delegation would include top officials from the department of foreign affairs, Mandela's office, the defence force and the secretariat that oversees security forces.

U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali has said he expected more than 12 countries to provide troops and equipment for a Canadian-led force to open up aid routes to starving Rwandan and Burundian refugees in Zaire.
Thousands of the refugees have fled Zaire by lake and land to Tanzania.
Other countries considering participation or contributions to the humanitarian force are France, the United States, Belgium, Britain, Germany, the Netherlands, Ireland and Finland.
